title: QTc stacking: BDQ, CFZ, FQ, DLM
dek: Several Group A/B/C drugs prolong QT. Adding them is arithmetic on an ECG, not a surprise. Electrolytes, companion CYP3A4 inhibitors, and a stop rule belong on the same plate.
story: Bedaquiline, clofazimine, moxifloxacin (more than levofloxacin), and delamanid all prolong the QT interval. BPaLM stacks BDQ+Mfx. BDLLfxC can stack BDQ+DLM+CFZ+Lfx. This is expected pharmacology. Baseline ECG, repeat ECGs (programmes often week 2, 4, 8, 12, then monthly), and potassium/magnesium repletion are the monitoring, not an afterthought.

QTcF (Fridericia) is the usual correction. Absolute QTcF ≥500 ms or a large Δ from baseline is a hold/review threshold in most handbooks — look up the current operational cut, do not invent one from a blog. Drop the most dispensable QT drug first (often the FQ if BDQ is load-bearing, or CFZ in a five-drug Pa-sparing start).
CYP3A4 inhibitors (some azoles, macrolides, cobicistat) raise BDQ and sometimes DLM. Ondansetron and methadone add QT. The TB regimen is not the only line on the med rec.
deepTitle: Congenital long QT and the unmeasured ECG
deep: A family history of sudden death is a BDQ counselling item.
Moxifloxacin’s QT effect is why some HPMZ programmes still want a baseline ECG in older adults — DS-TB is not QT-free if an FQ is in the acronym.
Linezolid is not a QT drug; it is a marrow/nerve drug. Do not skip CBC because you did an ECG.
Portable ECG quality is data. A sloppy QTc is how people get denied BDQ incorrectly.

visual.caption: Schematic QTcF distributions: baseline, plus one QT drug, plus a stack. The right tail is the stop-rule neighbourhood, not the mean.

example.title: QTcF 512 on BDLLfxC week 4
example.setup: Pregnant RR, BDLLfxC, K 3.1, QTcF 512 ms. FQ DST still pending.

steps.title: Replete K/Mg now
steps.body: Do not first-stop BDQ for a potassium problem.

steps.title: Repeat ECG after repletion
steps.body: If still ≥500, drop the most dispensable QT agent.

steps.title: If FQ-S later, CFZ was already the prune
steps.body: If FQ-R, Lfx goes; CFZ stays — plan that fork before the panic.

example.takeaway: QT management is electrolytes plus which letter you can actually drop.

check.prompt: Which list is the usual TB QT stack?
check.why: LZD is marrow/nerve. Aminoglycosides are ears/kidneys.

check.prompt: A commonly used hold-and-review QTcF neighbourhood is:
choices: ≥500 ms (or a large Δ from baseline) — confirm in the current handbook
600 as the mean of healthy adults
check.answer: ≥500 ms (or a large Δ from baseline) — confirm in the current handbook
check.why: Means sit near 400. The right tail is the rule.

whyWrong.200 ms: Not compatible with life as QTc.

check.prompt: On the density-shift plate, stacking QT drugs is drawn as:
choices: A left shift of the mean
A right shift of the QTcF distribution (longer interval)
check.answer: A right shift of the QTcF distribution (longer interval)
check.why: Prolongation is a rightward mean. The danger is the overlapping tail past 500.
